Subject: DPA annex - operator access & customer keys

Rishi,

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Ferngate's counsel has a couple of follow-ups as we review Redwood's private-deploy (VPC/on-prem) annex. Primary asks: can you confirm (1) whether operator accounts used for orchestration/patching have any ability to decrypt tenant data when customer-managed keys are in use, and (2) what the handback process looks like if we terminate (keystore return + operator telemetry purge).

We attached the draft annex with a few inline redlines for clarity. From our side we need firm language in the DPA that:
- Operator privileges are limited to non-decrypting maintenance tasks
- Any emergency break-glass process requires recorded, auditable, customer-approved steps
- Key escrow/handback mechanics and timelines (preferably 30 days post-termination)

Appreciate a note on whether Redwood can accept those constraints or offer alternative wording.

Best,
Maya Linton
Legal, Ferngate Systems

Maya —

Thanks for the redline and the clear list. Short answers up front:
1) Operator accounts: when customer-managed keys (BYOK) are in place, operator accounts do NOT have the ability to decrypt tenant data. Our runtime separates the keystore (customer KMS) from the operator management plane and we only hold authorization tokens for provisioning/ops; no plaintext keys or decrypt calls are performed by operator tools.

2) Break-glass / emergency process: we support a documented break-glass that requires a joint approval flow (customer primary + Redwood security lead) and is fully audited. We can include a step-by-step runbook as an annex.

3) Handback and purge: Redwood will return any escrow material and provide an export of operational logs within 30 days. We can commit to a 90-day retention for audit data unless otherwise required by regulation; we will provide attestations of log deletion once purge is complete.

I've attached an internal Operator Access Matrix and a lightly edited version of your annex with suggested wording for the "no-decrypt" and "break-glass" clauses. Please confirm if the edits map to your expectations or if you want a redline that is more prescriptive.

Next steps: Monica, Karthik — can you review the proposed clauses I attached and flag anything that might still expose us operationally?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Rishi / Karthik —

Quick read of Rishi's edits. Overall they're conservative and map to what our private-deploy architecture supports. A few internal clarifications we should tighten before sending back to Ferngate:
- "Operator accounts do not decrypt data": change to "Operator accounts do not possess cryptographic material or rights to perform tenant-data decryption under normal operations". This avoids implying a technical impossibility in disaster recovery scenarios.
- Break-glass: add explicit SLA for acknowledging a break-glass request (e.g., 4 hours) and require out-of-band confirmation (phone + signed request) for any decryption step.
- Escrow/handback: propose 30 days for return of material; propose 45 days for full telemetry purge with attestations signed by Redwood security.

Karthik — please add any guardrails about operator tooling (e.g., ephemeral maintenance sessions, no persistent key caches, least-privilege ACLs).

-- Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Security Programs | Redwood Inference

Thanks — addendums from infra/security:

- Technical guarantee: we will not persist customer plaintext keys or KMS materials in Redwood control plane. All maintenance tooling performs administrative actions via short-lived tokens; those tokens do not allow cryptographic operations against tenant ciphertext.
- Ephemeral sessions: any operator console session required for debugging will be time-limited (max 30 minutes) and can only be initiated with a two-person approval (Redwood engineer + Redwood security reviewer) and customer consent if keys are involved. Session recordings are retained according to the telemetry schedule and provided as part of the handback package.
- Telemetry purge: we can commit to a 45-day purge for operational telemetry related to customer environments, subject to preservation for legal/regulatory holds. We propose an attestation format (signed PDF) for the deletion event.

I'll prepare suggested DPA language for these points and drop into the redline.

— Karthik
